classification.difficultyReason: Find different rectangular arrangements of 16 unit tiles and compare their perimeters.

content.prompt: Imagine you have 16 tiles, each 1 cm square. Draw on grid paper some different rectangles that use all 16 tiles. You know that the area of each rectangle you have drawn is $16\text{ cm}^2$. What is the perimeter of each rectangle, in centimetres?

answer.short:
$1\text{ cm}\times16\text{ cm}$: $34\text{ cm}$; $2\text{ cm}\times8\text{ cm}$: $20\text{ cm}$; $4\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$: $16\text{ cm}$.

Arrange the tiles in rectangular rows, then add the four side lengths.
answer.worked:
The different rectangular arrangements have 1 row of 16 tiles, 2 rows of 8 tiles, or 4 rows of 4 tiles. Turning a rectangle does not give a different arrangement.

For the $1\text{ cm}\times16\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}P&=1+16+1+16\\P&=34\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
For the $2\text{ cm}\times8\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}P&=2+8+2+8\\P&=20\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
For the $4\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ square:
$$\begin{align*}P&=4+4+4+4\\P&=16\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
